notes: The harness accepts one connection and does not expose all connection attempts or client pool policy; no MUST-level same-connection assertion is invented.

requirement: Clients may replace connections for stream-ID exhaustion or connection errors
notes: The one-accepted-connection fixture cannot assert replacement/retry outcomes across sockets. TLS rekeying is separately excluded.

requirement: A server may terminate idle connections when necessary
notes: Idle policy is not configurable; no minimum lifetime or sleep-based acceptance condition is invented.

requirement: Before choosing to close TCP send GOAWAY so peers can identify processed streams
notes: No graceful target close operation independent of resource teardown is exposed; error cases permit absent best-effort GOAWAY and do not claim this recommendation is covered.

requirement: A cleartext connection may be reused for multiple authorities resolving to the same address
notes: RequestData cannot independently control target DNS resolution/authority selection and observe pool connection choice; no cross-origin reuse is required.

requirement: HTTPS cross-origin reuse requires the certificate to satisfy checks for the new host
notes: TLS certificate validation and ALPN are outside the plaintext prior-knowledge baseline.

requirement: Different SNI or client certificates can justify multiple same-address connections
notes: TLS identity configuration is outside the baseline; it is not treated as a failure of the single-connection recommendation.

requirement: Requests to an HTTP/2 proxy reuse the connection to that proxy
notes: Forwarding and proxy operation are outside the origin client/server baseline.

requirement: A server can use 421 when it does not wish a connection reused for an authority
notes: General 421 application semantics and origin/pool selection are not covered by a framing-only Reply status response.
